_README: RiboMine on LRZ CoolMUC-4 (SLURM). Submit from a login node with:
This is an ORDINARY RiboMine config -- `ribomine run -c` accepts it as-is.
The `_slurm` block below is a comment as far as RiboMine is concerned (config.py
ignores every key starting with '_'); it is read by slurm/master.sh alone. Keeping
it here means the cluster shape and the pipeline settings cannot drift apart.
BEFORE THE FIRST SUBMIT, check the three `reference` paths below. slurm/prep.sh
validates them and fails in minutes rather than letting a 24 h job die on a typo.

_slurm._: Read by slurm/master.sh only. 2 jobs x 4 nodes x 112 cores = 896 cores.
_limits: cm4_std: 2-4 nodes PER JOB (max 448 cores), 2 jobs running at once, 24 h.
So 896 cores is not one job -- it is an ARRAY OF 2, each 4 nodes wide.
cm4 nodes: 112 physical cores, 488 GiB, exclusive on cm4_std.

project.name: ribomine-lrz
_workdir: The ROOT. Per-node workdirs are <workdir>/shards/work_NN -- one per node, so
the eight `ribomine run` processes never write the same file. slurm/merge.sh
then builds <workdir>/merged/, from which the cohort-wide tables are written.
Heavy I/O, so DSS (not $HOME): a 500-run cohort moves several TB through here.
_jobs: 28 x 8 = 224 = the node's LOGICAL core count (112 physical + hyperthreads),
so this is deliberately twice as many samples in flight as there are physical
cores. It should be: the stage spends much of its time blocked on an ENA
download, and a sample that is waiting on the network is not using a core --
the other 27 can. Oversubscription is the point, not an accident.
It costs memory, though: ~28 GB for the node's one shared STAR genome plus
roughly 8 GB per sample in flight, so budget ~250 GB of the node's 480 GB.
If a node starts swapping, this is the number to cut.

_end: Set to 'qc' for the cheap first pass: it streams a 200k-read sample per run
instead of downloading anything, so a whole archive-wide screen costs hours
rather than days, and tells you how many of the hits are real Ribo-seq before
you spend a cohort's worth of bandwidth on them. Then set it to 'bam' and
resubmit -- resume reuses every QC verdict.

reference._: CHECK THESE. The STAR index must have been built with --sjdbGTFfile, or there is no gene-count matrix (prep.sh says so if it was not).

_connections: PER RUN -- and 28 runs download at once on each of 8 nodes, so the sockets
open against ENA at peak are 8 nodes * 28 runs * this. At 4 that is ~900,
already a lot to point at one host; RiboMine's own default of 8 would be
~1800. Lowering it costs less than it looks: the per-run connection count
exists to beat ENA's ~12 MB/s per-stream cap, and with 224 runs already in
flight the link saturates long before any single one of them does.
If downloads start failing (they show up in failed.tsv and in
mapping_summary.tsv), this is still the first knob to turn -- downwards.
